subject: Re: Urgent: Request for penetration test report and remediation status
messages:
From: Jordan Brooks <jordan.brooks@bluecrest.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@bluecrest.com
Date: 2026-06-22T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Pen test report and remediation details (urgent)

Hi Kimberly,

We experienced a spike in anomalous API activity yesterday that triggered an internal review. Our security team would like to review Redwood's most recent penetration test report and a remediation status overview for any findings that could be relevant to the event.

Specifically, we need:
- The latest pen test report (redacted is fine if sensitive details are removed)
- A matrix of findings -> remediation status and dates
- Any relevant logs or telemetry slices you can provide for 2026-06-21 00:00 - 2026-06-21 23:59 UTC

Can you confirm whether you can share a redacted report and the remediation tracker by EOD today? If not, please advise the earliest ETA and whether we need an NDA/POA to access more detailed artifacts.

Thanks,
Jordan Brooks
Senior Security Engineer
BlueCrest Health

---

(attachment: incident_alert_screencap.png - image/png)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Brooks <jordan.brooks@bluecrest.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-22T10:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Pen test report and remediation details (urgent)

Hi Jordan — thanks for the heads up and sorry to hear you had that noise. We take these requests seriously and will prioritize. A few quick notes up front:

- We can provide a redacted copy of our most recent external penetration test report (Q3 2024) and an internal remediation tracker that maps findings to fixes, owners, and deployment dates.
- Full, unredacted findings (exploit PoCs, exact payloads, and vuln proofs) require an evidence-sharing review and are typically provided under a mutual NDA / controlled-access Drive folder. If BlueCrest needs that level of detail, we can expedite the approval.
- For the immediate ask, I can share a redacted PDF + remediation_tracker.csv and a Drive link to SOC 2 artifacts that may help with control evidence.

I’m attaching a redacted report and our remediation tracker extract for the items we think are most relevant. Rishi — can you add a short remediation summary in-line with timelines so we can set expectations? Lauren/Marissa — loop in CS or legal if BlueCrest requests unredacted materials or a formal accreditation packet.

If that works, we can also schedule a 30-minute call today to walk the BlueCrest team through the redactions and timeline.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference
(attachment stubs: redwood_pen_test_2024Q3_redacted.pdf, remediation_tracker_20240601.csv)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Jordan Brooks <jordan.brooks@bluecrest.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-22T14:42:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Pen test report and remediation details (technical summary)

Jordan / Kimberly — quick technical note from the remediation side:

Summary of high-level items (from Q3 2024 pen test) and current state: 
- Auth session fixation (Finding ID: P-2024-07) — mitigated in 2024-11 by rotating session tokens and adding stricter cookie flags. Verified in staging; deployed to prod 2024-11-18.
- Excessive permissions on internal management endpoint (Finding ID: P-2024-09) — access control tightened (RBAC) and endpoint removed where not required. Deployed 2025-02-03; residual monitoring rules added.
- Dependency vulnerability (high severity, third-party lib) — upgraded and backported fixes, patch deployed 2025-05-12.

For the event window you shared (2026-06-21), we’ve pulled the following artifacts that we can share under controlled access:
- Redacted access logs (token hashes only, no full tokens) covering 2026-06-21 00:00–23:59 UTC
- Request path aggregation showing unusual spike by client_id (we can map to your client_id off-band)
- SIEM correlation summary (we will not share raw internal SIEM pulls without an NDA)

Per Kimberly’s note, I’ve updated remediation_tracker_20240601.csv with columns: finding_id, owner, status, remediation_date, verification_notes. All P2/P1 items in that tracker were patched prior to 2026 and are marked as verified.

If BlueCrest needs CVE references or PoC details, we will need a signed evidence sharing agreement. Happy to join a call to walk through the artifacts.

— Rishi
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Brooks <jordan.brooks@bluecrest.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@bluecrest.com
Date: 2026-06-23T08:30:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Pen test report and remediation details (follow-up)

Kimberly / Rishi — thanks for the quick responses and the attachments. A couple of follow-ups before we escalate internally:

1) Can you provide specific CVE identifiers and the associated remediation commit IDs for the dependency vulnerability you mentioned? Our compliance team needs traceability.
2) The redacted logs are helpful — can you include a 10-line sample (with timestamps) showing the anomalous requests (remove any customer PII)?
3) We understand PoC details require an NDA. Can you send a link to your standard Evidence Sharing Agreement / DocuSign? We’ll route it to legal immediately if needed.

If we can get points 1–3 within 24 hours, that will likely satisfy the initial rush and prevent an Exec-level escalation. If not, we’ll need to ask for an on-the-record briefing with a security leader.

Appreciate the responsiveness.
Jordan
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Brooks <jordan.brooks@bluecrest.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-23T09:10:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Pen test report and remediation details (materials shared)

Jordan — thanks, and understood. Deliverables attached and notes below:

- redwood_pen_test_2024Q3_redacted.pdf (attached) — redactions remove PoC payloads and tester accounts per our disclosure policy; we kept finding IDs and remediation summaries intact.
- remediation_tracker_20240601.csv (attached) — includes finding_id => remediation_commit (SHA truncated), remediation_date, verification_notes.
- 10-line sample log (redacted) — included in the Drive folder (link below) as sample_logs_20260621.txt. Sample contains only hashed token, timestamp, request_path, response_code.
- Evidence Sharing Agreement (DocuSign): https://docusign.com/example-evidence-agreement?id=EVID-2026-5432
- Drive evidence folder (controlled access): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example-redwood-evidence

If BlueCrest legal signs the DocuSign link, we’ll provision the controlled Drive folder that contains full log slices and PoC write-ups under an access expiration policy. If you’d like, I can set up a 30-minute bridge with Rishi and me to walk the log sample and the remediation commit references.

Respectfully,
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference
(attachments: redwood_pen_test_2024Q3_redacted.pdf, remediation_tracker_20240601.csv)
